short: A king of Macedon who conquered the Persian Empire and created one of the largest empires of the ancient world.
full:
Succeeding his father Philip II in 336 BCE at the age of twenty, Alexander secured his position in Greece before launching a massive military campaign against the Achaemenid Persian Empire. Undefeated in battle, he led his armies across Asia Minor, Egypt, and Persia, eventually reaching the Indus Valley. He founded over twenty cities bearing his name, most notably Alexandria in Egypt.

Alexander died in Babylon in 323 BCE at age thirty-two, before he could consolidate his vast realm. His death triggered the Wars of the Diadochi, tearing his empire apart into rival Hellenistic kingdoms, but his conquests permanently spread Greek culture and language across the Middle East and Asia.
